benchmark: LongMemEval recall sweep: the window gate, timed with a stand-in cross-encoder
commit: ccec496 (library src/ as at that commit; the bench's rerankGate as on this branch)
why: Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 could not be downloaded in the sandbox this ran in (huggingface.co blocked). The cached Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 has the identical encoder (BERT, 6 layers, hidden 384, 12 heads, FFN 1536, 512 positions, the same uncased vocabulary); the cross-encoder only adds a 384-to-1 head. Scoring the same question-passage pairs, tokenized and batched (16) as LocalReranker does, costs the same forward passes. Its scores are meaningless, so this file holds time and, for questions that name no period, the rounds; not evidence gained.
method: A scratch copy of recall-sweep.mjs's loop (not committed): each question's history built once (SqliteMemoryStore over node:sqlite, the sandbox cannot load better-sqlite3), then four arms recall from it with a fresh HybridRetriever each, in rotating order, the median of 3 recalls per arm and question: none; the stand-in at rerankDepth 30 behind rerankGate(lib, instance, 'window'); content-words; content-words plus the gated stand-in. Settings as published: expand { now: question_date }, limit 100, 20 rounds shown (40 when counting). fp32 weights (q8 is not cached).
